cards.title: LARC: Latent Continuous-Space Reasoning Boosts Unified Multimodal Image Generation
cards.why_it_matters: Closes a fundamental gap between discrete CoT reasoning and continuous image generation — directly relevant to anyone building or evaluating multimodal models.
cards.summary: LARC frames reasoning for image generation in continuous hidden-state space rather than discrete tokens, using two-stage training: curriculum SFT to shift from token-level to latent reasoning, then information-gain RL for self-supervised refinement. On GenEval it achieves a 7 percentage-point gain over BAGEL and shows measurable test-time scaling under both parallel and sequential strategies.

cards.title: Flide: Up to 9.5× Faster LLM Decision-Tree Inference via Exact State Forking
cards.why_it_matters: Directly solves inference inefficiency for tree-structured agent decision models — important for anyone building or deploying LLM-based agent systems at scale.
cards.summary: Flide is an inference engine for decision models that decouples logical tree structure from a flattened physical token stream. ForkAttention uses GPU-resident indices to ensure each branch evaluates identically to an isolated forward pass, covering both standard attention and recurrent GatedDeltaNet layers. Benchmarks show up to 9.5× speedup over vLLM and SGLang with the closest match to float32 reference in total variation distance.

cards.title: Latent Sparse Attention (LSA) Enables Subquadratic Accuracy at 10M-Token Context
cards.why_it_matters: Practical subquadratic attention that maintains accuracy at extreme context lengths is a key infrastructure need for long-horizon agent and research workflows.
cards.summary: LSA hierarchically clusters keys in a learned latent space so queries score cluster hierarchies rather than all keys, reducing prefill, decode, and training cost. Distilled-LSA on GLM-5.3-FLASH at 10M tokens speeds up one attention layer 22.7× in prefill and 4.6× in decode over original sparse attention; on QWEN-3.8-27B the gains are 72.4× and 42.5× over full attention. Native-LSA matches full-attention accuracy with 1.6× training speedup at 128k tokens.

cards.title: ID-WM: Hierarchical World Model Separates Reachability Planning from Low-Level Control
cards.why_it_matters: A principled hierarchical world model that reduces compounding errors in long-horizon tasks — directly relevant to embodied AI and model-based RL research.
cards.summary: ID-WM uses a high-level model to sample reachable state transitions across the manifold and a low-level inverse dynamics solver to ground them into actions, avoiding rigid macro-actions. This separation lets the planner find feasible subgoals without low-level execution constraints. Results show a 38.5% improvement over SOTA policy and diffusion-based planners and a 135% gain over single-level world model MPC on long-horizon navigation and manipulation tasks.

cards.title: Secret-Shared Teleportation of a Two-Qudit Gate with Deferred Recipient Selection
cards.why_it_matters: Advances distributed quantum computing by enabling flexible, post-distribution routing of entangling gate capability — a meaningful primitive for quantum networks.
cards.summary: The paper shows a two-qudit entangling gate (CSUM^k) can be secret-shared across n parties: shares distributed in advance, with a later key release activating exactly one recipient. Any coalition fewer than n nodes or the key register alone learns nothing; unselected nodes cannot detect selection. The two-candidate case forms a ((3,5)) threshold scheme with explicit O(n) encoder/decoder circuits.

cards.title: RoboArchitect: Automated LLM-Driven Agent Harness Design Replaces Robotic Finetuning
cards.why_it_matters: Demonstrates that frozen policy performance can be dramatically recovered through automated harness optimization — a compelling alternative to expensive finetuning that reshapes how researchers think about robot adaptation.
cards.summary: RoboArchitect uses a coding model to observe robot rollouts, diagnose failures, and iteratively revise the agent harness around a frozen policy — including evolving persistent memory for learned heuristics like effective grasp depths. Without any weight updates, success rates rise from 9.7% to 43.3% on unseen scenes and 12.7% to 40.2% on unseen tasks across multiple benchmarks, often matching or exceeding finetuned baselines.
